question: How should a midwife best respond when a community relies heavily on traditional birth attendants?

options.A: Report all community elders to the police immediately
options.B: Forbid pregnant women from speaking to traditional healers
options.C: Ignore the community and close the local health post
options.D: Engage respectfully and build referral linkages with them

explanation: Collaborative engagement and respectful communication with traditional birth attendants achieve much better maternal outcomes than confrontation. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T3#BMP117_U1_T3_h4)

question: A village chief hesitates to allow an outreach clinic because he fears outside interference. What is the best step for the midwife?

options.A: Visit him respectfully ahead of time to explain community health benefits
options.B: Report him to the police for obstructing health services
options.C: Ignore his concerns and set up the clinic equipment anyway
options.D: Move the outreach site to a neighboring hostile village

explanation: Respectful dialogue and clear communication help build trust and secure the cooperation of influential local leaders. [learn more](BMP227_U1_T1#BMP227_U1_T1_h2)

question: What makes Solar Direct Drive (SDD) refrigerators so helpful for remote Nigerian health posts?

options.A: They automatically reconstitute dry vaccine vials
options.B: They double as domestic food freezers for staff members
options.C: They require no sunlight during the entire rainy season
options.D: They operate without expensive or fragile battery storage banks

explanation: SDD units use solar energy directly to freeze water linings, eliminating reliance on short-lived batteries that frequently fail in rural clinics. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T4#BMP117_U3_T4_h3)

question: How does magnesium interact with calcium during muscle contraction?

options.A: It stops calcium from ever entering the bloodstream
options.B: It binds directly to calcium to make bones rigid
options.C: It mimics calcium to cause continuous muscle cramps
options.D: It acts as a natural antagonist to promote muscle relaxation

explanation: While calcium helps muscles contract, magnesium blocks calcium channels so muscle fibers can relax. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T8#BMP118_U2_T8_h2)

question: What physical sign indicates a Grade 2 goiter during a routine neck check in antenatal care?

options.A: The thyroid is completely invisible and cannot be felt by hand
options.B: The swelling can only be felt when the woman swallows water
options.C: The swelling is clearly visible with the neck in a normal position
options.D: The swelling only appears when the woman extends her neck backward

explanation: A Grade 2 goiter is large enough to be seen easily without needing to feel the neck or tilt the head back. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T5#BMP118_U4_T5_h4)

question: What does a flattened or blanched nipple look like immediately after a feed?

options.A: It looks squeezed and lacks normal color
options.B: It is covered in thick yellow pus
options.C: It remains completely unchanged
options.D: It appears swollen and bright red

explanation: Blanching and a lipstick-like shape show that the baby pinched the tissue against the hard palate during feeding. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T5#BMP214_U3_T5_h3)

question: Which transport process uses cellular energy to move substances against a concentration gradient?

options.A: Active transport
options.B: Facilitated diffusion
options.C: Osmosis
options.D: Simple diffusion

explanation: Active transport uses energy to move molecules from an area of lower concentration to an area of higher concentration. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T3#BMP121_U2_T3_h3)

question: In the BUBBLE-EE postnatal check system, what does the letter 'L' stand for?

options.A: Lochia
options.B: Lactation
options.C: Labor
options.D: Ligaments

explanation: In the BUBBLE-EE acronym, L stands for lochia, which is the normal vaginal discharge after childbirth. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T1#BMP218_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why must you evaluate and document whether a pain relief method actually worked?

options.A: To confirm whether the method helped the mother cope with contractions
options.B: To ensure the patient stays asleep until the second stage begins
options.C: To replace the need for charting vital signs on the partograph
options.D: To prove that medication costs can be billed at a higher rate

explanation: Documenting the response lets you know if the current pain relief is working or if you need to try a different approach to support the mother. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T5#BMP212_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which hormone relaxes the smooth muscles in blood vessel walls during pregnancy?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles throughout the body, including vein walls, making them more prone to stretching. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T14#BMP212_U1_T14_h2)

question: What type of preparation is the standard chickenpox vaccine?

options.A: Purified bacterial toxin
options.B: Live-attenuated virus
options.C: Recombinant protein subunit
options.D: Killed whole bacteria

explanation: The chickenpox vaccine contains a weakened form of the live virus, which safely trains the immune system without causing the full illness. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T4#BMP222_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why do midwives advise pregnant women to avoid using sodium bicarbonate for routine heartburn?

options.A: It instantly stops all uterine blood flow
options.B: It turns stomach acid into dangerous poison
options.C: It contains high levels of sodium that can cause fluid retention
options.D: It causes permanent damage to the throat

explanation: Excess sodium intake can worsen swelling and fluid overload during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T11#BMP212_U1_T11_h5)

question: What happens to maternal stores of omega-3 fatty acids if a pregnant woman eats a diet very low in these nutrients?

options.A: The placenta will block all fat transfer to protect the mother
options.B: The pregnancy will instantly halt until she changes her diet
options.C: The fetus will draw omega-3s directly from maternal tissue stores
options.D: The mother's body will automatically manufacture new omega-3s from sugar

explanation: The developing fetus prioritizes nutrient acquisition, meaning it will deplete maternal reserves of essential fatty acids if dietary intake is lacking. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T3#BMP118_U2_T3_h3)

question: A pregnant woman at 28 weeks visits the clinic with sudden breathlessness, trembling, and a feeling of doom that pass in ten minutes. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Perform a clinical assessment to evaluate for panic attacks while checking vital signs
options.B: Tell her it is just normal pregnancy fatigue and send her home
options.C: Prepare her for immediate emergency cesarean section
options.D: Diagnose her with chronic depression without further questions

explanation: Taking a careful history and checking vitals helps identify panic while ensuring no physical emergency is missed. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T5#BMP223_U3_T5_h3)

question: What term describes the birth of an abnormally large baby, often linked to maternal diabetes?

options.A: Microcephaly
options.B: Hydrocephalus
options.C: Macrosomia
options.D: Apgar syndrome

explanation: Macrosomia refers to a newborn with an excessive birth weight, commonly defined as over 4,000 grams. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T7#BMP118_U4_T7_h4)

question: Taking tramadol along with which type of drug carries a major risk of dangerous serotonin syndrome?

options.A: Standard magnesium sulfate therapy
options.B: Routine prenatal iron supplements
options.C: Over-the-counter antacids
options.D: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs)

explanation: Combining tramadol with MAOIs can trigger dangerous serotonin toxicity because of tramadol's dual action on neurotransmitters. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T3#BMP213_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is a vital safety component taught to clients during self-injection training for Sayana Press?

options.A: Mixing the hormone powder with sterile water
options.B: Boiling the needle before reuse
options.C: Storing the pre-filled device in a freezer
options.D: Safe needle disposal in a safety box

explanation: Clients must learn proper disposal of used devices to prevent needlestick injuries and environmental contamination at home. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T6#BMP224_U3_T6_h8)

question: Why are immunization visits considered valuable opportunities for spotting developmental issues?

options.A: Parents are legally required to report milestones during vaccination
options.B: They bring healthy infants into the clinic for routine contact at regular ages
options.C: Vaccines directly stimulate brain cells to improve motor coordination
options.D: Midwives have extra time during injections to complete full psychological tests

explanation: Routine immunization schedules ensure that growing infants return to the primary health clinic at predictable ages, making surveillance convenient. [learn more](BMP222_U1_T4#BMP222_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary role of diuretic medications in treating heart failure?

options.A: To widen narrowed coronary arteries instantly
options.B: To remove excess fluid and relieve congestion
options.C: To cure underlying heart valve infections
options.D: To speed up a dangerously slow heart rate

explanation: Diuretics help the kidneys eliminate sodium and water, reducing the fluid overload that causes congestion. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T5#BMP125_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is another name for democratic leadership in the ward?

options.A: Autocratic leadership
options.B: Transactional leadership
options.C: Laissez-faire leadership
options.D: Participative leadership

explanation: Democratic leadership is also called participative leadership because the manager invites the team to take part in making decisions. [learn more](BMP312_U1_T9#BMP312_U1_T9_h1)

question: Which postpartum patient faces the highest risk for developing a direct surgical site infection?

options.A: A mother who experienced a spontaneous birth
options.B: A healthy mother discharged after six hours
options.C: An antenatal client waiting for her scan
options.D: A mother recovering from a caesarean section

explanation: Surgical incisions break the protective skin barrier, creating a primary entry route for pathogens compared to an intact perineum after normal birth. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is an essential daily nursing task for a hospital patient dealing with severe abdominal swelling from fluid (ascites)?

options.A: Testing visual acuity using a Snellen chart
options.B: Performing active range of motion exercises
options.C: Weighing the patient and measuring abdominal girth
options.D: Checking deep tendon reflexes every two hours

explanation: Checking the patient's weight and measuring their belly size daily helps nurses track if fluid is building up or clearing out. [learn more](BMP125_U4_T2#BMP125_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is the standard initial fluid bolus volume per kilogram for a severely dehydrated child in shock?

options.A: 20 mL/kg
options.B: 10 mL/kg
options.C: 50 mL/kg
options.D: 5 mL/kg

explanation: Emergency fluid resuscitation for severe dehydration starts with a rapid infusion of twenty milliliters per kilogram of an isotonic solution. [learn more](BMP222_U3_T4#BMP222_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is a direct consequence for a midwife who breaches national data protection regulations?

options.A: Immediate exemption from future annual licensing fees
options.B: Automatic promotion to a hospital management position
options.C: Potential disciplinary action and license suspension
options.D: Free upgrade to premium hospital software tools

explanation: Violating data protection laws carries legal and professional penalties that can halt a clinician's ability to practice. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T4#BMP123_U5_T4_h5)

question: What is it called when the placenta separates, but the blood is trapped inside with no external bleeding?

options.A: Revealed abruption
options.B: Marginal abruption
options.C: Mixed abruption
options.D: Concealed abruption

explanation: In a concealed abruption, the edges of the placenta remain attached or the membranes trap the blood, preventing it from showing outside. [learn more](BMP221_U2_T3#BMP221_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why are antenatal and postnatal clinics ideal settings for identifying survivors of gender-based violence?

options.A: Clinics are completely free from cultural biases and stigma
options.B: Midwives are legally required to arrest suspected abusers on site
options.C: Patients are always accompanied by independent legal counsel
options.D: Women attend these clinics regularly during pregnancy and after birth

explanation: Routine maternity care brings women into contact with health workers multiple times, creating opportunities to build trust and screen for abuse. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T4#BMP310_U1_T4_h5)

question: How do electronic clinical decision support tools assist midwives during antenatal care?

options.A: By automatically prescribing medications without a doctor
options.B: By generating alerts for potential allergies or abnormal vitals
options.C: By replacing physical examinations with remote sensors
options.D: By diagnosing complex surgical conditions independently

explanation: Decision support software flags critical warnings, such as a known drug allergy or rising blood pressure, helping midwives act quickly. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T2#BMP123_U5_T2_h2)

question: Which sign usually disappears first when a patient's magnesium sulfate level gets too high?

options.A: Spontaneous eye blinking
options.B: Deep tendon reflexes
options.C: Normal body temperature
options.D: Regular bowel sounds

explanation: Knee-jerk reflexes slow down and disappear before breathing problems or other serious signs of toxicity occur. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T7#BMP213_U1_T7_h4)

question: When can a mother with an uncomplicated vaginal birth generally start gentle walking and breathing exercises?

options.A: Immediately upon arrival at home from the labor ward
options.B: At least three months after the baby is born
options.C: Within the first twenty-four hours
options.D: Only after the six-week postnatal clinic visit

explanation: Early ambulation is safe and encouraged for normal vaginal births to prevent blood clots and promote recovery. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T4#BMP212_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recognized complication of severe zinc deficiency in pregnancy?

options.A: Permanent maternal vision loss
options.B: Intrauterine growth restriction
options.C: Prolonged or difficult labor
options.D: Premature rupture of membranes

explanation: While severe zinc deficiency causes growth restriction, prolonged labor, and membrane complications, permanent blindness is primarily associated with vitamin A deficiency, not zinc. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h6)

question: What is the standard mode of delivery planned for a persistent term transverse lie?

options.A: Vaginal breech extraction
options.B: Internal podalic version
options.C: Elective caesarean section
options.D: Vacuum-assisted delivery

explanation: A planned caesarean section prevents the life-threatening complications of obstructed labour associated with a transverse lie. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T6#BMP311_U1_T6_h6)

question: A pregnant woman tests positive for both HBsAg and HBeAg. What does the HBeAg result tell you?

options.A: Her baby is completely protected from infection
options.B: She is fully immune and cannot pass the virus
options.C: She has a high viral load and high infectivity
options.D: She has cleared the virus from her liver permanently

explanation: HBeAg shows that the virus is multiplying quickly in the body, meaning the chance of passing it to the baby is high. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T7#BMP221_U4_T7_h3)

question: Why is fluid resuscitation usually started before giving insulin in a DKA emergency?

options.A: To raise the blood sugar high enough to counteract the insulin
options.B: To ensure the kidneys absorb all the insulin before it reaches the heart
options.C: To prevent a sudden drop in blood pressure caused by intravascular volume depletion
options.D: To make the patient feel comfortable before starting painful injections

explanation: Starting insulin without fluids causes glucose and water to move into cells, worsening intravascular dehydration and precipitating severe vascular collapse. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T3#BMP216_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common source of contamination in the operating theatre?

options.A: Air currents stirred up by excessive staff movement
options.B: Unsterile items touching the edges of a sterile table
options.C: Punctured surgical gloves unnoticed by the wearer
options.D: Using sterile instruments well within their expiry date

explanation: Properly sterilized instruments kept within date are safe and do not cause contamination. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T2#BMP116_U5_T2_h7)

question: What is true about the transverse diameter of the pelvic inlet in an android pelvis?

options.A: It remains completely equal from front to back
options.B: It expands significantly during the second stage of labor
options.C: It is narrow near the front and wide near the back
options.D: It is wide near the front and narrow near the back

explanation: The wedge shape pushes the widest transverse portion backward toward the sacrum, leaving little space at the front of the pelvis. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T4#BMP210_U1_T4_h3)

question: Relatives bring a dead snake to the clinic along with a snakebite patient. What should you do?

options.A: Throw the snake away immediately without looking at it.
options.B: Use the dead snake to demonstrate first aid techniques to the patient.
options.C: Warn everyone not to touch the head because reflex bites can still inject venom.
options.D: Examine the fangs closely with your bare hands to identify the species.

explanation: Even after a snake is dead, nerve reflexes can cause it to bite and release venom if handled carelessly. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T7#BMP110_U7_T7_h2)

question: Why are antibiotics prescribed during the management of post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis?

options.A: To stop the glomeruli from leaking protein into the urine
options.B: To dissolve blood clots blocking the tiny kidney tubules
options.C: To eradicate any remaining bacterial infection in the body
options.D: To lower the patient's blood pressure back to normal levels

explanation: Antibiotics clear out lingering streptococcal bacteria, though they do not reverse existing kidney inflammation directly. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T4#BMP216_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to effective clinical problem solving?

options.A: Poor handover notes and communication gaps
options.B: Cognitive bias and unverified assumptions
options.C: Adequate staffing and abundant medical supplies
options.D: Severe physical fatigue and mental burnout

explanation: Sufficient staff and supplies actually support and facilitate problem solving, whereas shortages and burnout act as barriers. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T9#BMP110_U3_T9_h4)

question: What kind of discharge is typical in bacterial vaginosis?

options.A: Bloody and clumpy
options.B: Thin, grayish-white, and smooth
options.C: Thick, white, and cottage-cheese-like
options.D: Frothy, yellow-green, and foul-smelling

explanation: Bacterial vaginosis typically causes a smooth, watery, grayish-white discharge that coats the area evenly. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h4)

question: What is a key part of community reintegration programs for VVF survivors?

options.A: Full exemption from community leadership roles
options.B: Mandatory relocation to a different state
options.C: Vocational training and skills acquisition
options.D: Assignment of permanent government housing

explanation: Learning a practical trade helps survivors earn their own money and rebuild their confidence after overcoming the condition. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T10#BMP310_U3_T10_h6)

question: Which tab on the PowerPoint ribbon is used to add pictures and video clips to a slide?

options.A: Insert tab
options.B: Design tab
options.C: Transition tab
options.D: Home tab

explanation: The Insert tab contains commands for adding external media such as pictures, shapes, audio, and video files. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T3#BMP123_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why is a patient who had a craniotomy for prolonged obstructed labor at high risk for a vesicovaginal fistula?

options.A: Pressure necrosis of tissues trapped between the fetal head and the pelvic bones
options.B: Aggressive postpartum use of high-dose oxytocin infusions to stop bleeding
options.C: Severe allergic reactions to the prophylactic antibiotics administered post-surgery
options.D: Direct laceration of the bladder dome by the obstetrician's perforating instrument

explanation: Prolonged compression cuts off blood supply to the bladder and vaginal walls, causing tissue death and subsequent fistula formation. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T5#BMP311_U3_T5_h5)

question: How do opposing lawyers typically use missing or messy entries during a malpractice lawsuit?

options.A: To prove the hospital has excellent administrative standards
options.B: To request a higher financial grant for the maternity unit
options.C: To argue negligence and lack of standard care by the midwife
options.D: To support the midwife's verbal testimony during cross-examination

explanation: Gaps and messy writing create doubt, allowing lawyers to convince the court that proper monitoring and interventions were neglected. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T3#BMP211_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why must midwives pay special attention to patients with a history of asthma when administering new drugs?

options.A: They absorb oral medications much faster than other patients.
options.B: Their lungs are already filled with fluid from previous infections.
options.C: They cannot feel the early skin symptoms of an allergic rash.
options.D: They are at higher risk for severe respiratory compromise during a reaction.

explanation: Asthmatic patients have hyper-reactive airways, meaning any allergic bronchospasm can quickly become severe and life-threatening. [learn more](BMP120_U2_T7#BMP120_U2_T7_h4)

question: Why is adequate fluid intake especially important for a breastfeeding mother?

options.A: It supports adequate milk production
options.B: It stops uterine involution from occurring
options.C: It eliminates the need for perineal care
options.D: It completely prevents postpartum depression

explanation: Breast milk is largely composed of water, so nursing mothers must drink enough fluids to maintain their supply. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T4#BMP218_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which section occupies the topmost part of the standard WHO partograph sheet?

options.A: Neonatal immunization records
options.B: Postpartum family planning notes
options.C: Maternal blood pressure logs
options.D: Fetal condition monitoring

explanation: The top section of the chart is dedicated to tracking the baby's heart rate, liquor status, and head molding. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T2#BMP211_U4_T2_h2)

question: A pregnant woman in a remote pre-colonial setting needed comfort during labor. What intervention was most likely used by her local birth attendant?

options.A: Electronic fetal heart rate monitoring
options.B: Intravenous fluid therapy
options.C: Cesarean section under general anesthesia
options.D: Abdominal massage and local herbs

explanation: Indigenous care relied on natural remedies, physical comfort measures like massage, and traditional support systems rather than modern medical technology. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h3)

question: What 24-hour urine protein level is typically used to define nephrotic syndrome in adults?

options.A: Between 1.0 and 2.0 grams
options.B: Exactly 500 milligrams
options.C: Less than 0.5 grams
options.D: Greater than 3.5 grams

explanation: Losing more than 3.5 grams of protein in a 24-hour urine collection is a key diagnostic sign of nephrotic syndrome. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T5#BMP216_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why is simple reassurance from the midwife so powerful for a woman experiencing baby blues?

options.A: It relieves her fear that she is losing her mind
options.B: It forces her to stop crying within a few minutes
options.C: It immediately cures the underlying hormonal imbalance
options.D: It replaces the need for any family support system

explanation: Many women fear their sudden sadness means they are mentally unstable; knowing it is a common, temporary phase brings immense relief. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T1#BMP223_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why should the mother move the baby to the breast rather than leaning her breast down toward the baby?

options.A: The baby will refuse to open its mouth if the breast moves
options.B: Gravity pulls the milk out of the ducts too quickly
options.C: Moving the breast stops the let-down reflex from occurring
options.D: Leaning forward causes poor spinal posture and a shallow, painful latch

explanation: Leaning down strains the mother's back and usually results in an off-center, shallow attachment that damages the nipple. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T2#BMP214_U3_T2_h3)

question: What main sign separates eclampsia from pre-eclampsia?

options.A: A sudden drop in maternal body temperature
options.B: The presence of generalized convulsions
options.C: The total absence of protein in the urine
options.D: Severe swelling of the upper eyelids

explanation: Eclampsia is diagnosed when a pregnant woman with pre-eclampsia experiences unexplained generalized seizures. [learn more](BMP221_U3_T5#BMP221_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why is diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) in an expectant mother so dangerous for the baby?

options.A: The placenta stores excess ketones and releases them to the fetus
options.B: High glucose levels cause the fetus to stop growing completely
options.C: Maternal ketones destroy the umbilical cord blood vessels instantly
options.D: Maternal acidosis quickly reduces blood flow through the placenta

explanation: Severe acid-base imbalance in the mother compromises uteroplacental perfusion, cutting off oxygen and nutrients to the baby. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T3#BMP216_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a common physical symptom of advanced gynecological cancers?

options.A: Severe pelvic or abdominal pain from nerve compression
options.B: Uncontrollable polyuria caused by type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.C: Chronic fatigue and progressive physical weakness
options.D: Lower limb lymphedema resulting from lymph node dissection

explanation: Type 1 diabetes is an endocrine condition, whereas the other options are direct physical complications or side effects of advanced pelvic tumors. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T6#BMP320_U2_T6_h3)

question: A newborn has a strong heart rate, pink body with blue hands and feet, active movement, and a good cry. What is the Apgar score?
explanation: A heart rate over 100 scores 2, pink body with blue extremities scores 1, active movement scores 2, and a good cry scores 2. This totals 9 because of the 1 point deduction for peripheral cyanosis. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T3#BMP212_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why must the body keep dissolved mineral ions in the blood tightly regulated?

options.A: Electrolytes are required to make white blood cells daily
options.B: High ion levels will turn all plasma proteins solid
options.C: Even small imbalances can disrupt nerve conduction and heart rhythm
options.D: Mineral ions are the only substances that provide energy

explanation: Nerves and muscles depend on balanced electrolyte levels to function correctly. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T1#BMP111_U5_T1_h4)

question: How should a midwife structure the synthesis of ten different research papers on postpartum hemorrhage?

options.A: Write a separate long paragraph for each author in alphabetical order
options.B: Group the papers by key themes like risk factors, prevention, and treatment
options.C: Combine all ten abstracts into one single paragraph without any changes
options.D: Focus only on the paper written by the most famous professor

explanation: Organizing by clinical themes allows you to compare what different authors say about the same specific issue. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T2#BMP225_U2_T2_h2)

question: What kind of budget expense covers expensive, long-lasting items like fetal monitors?

options.A: Capital expenditure
options.B: Operational cost
options.C: Personnel allowance
options.D: Recurring overhead

explanation: Capital expenditure refers to funds used to buy major physical equipment that stays in use for several years. [learn more](BMP312_U2_T3#BMP312_U2_T3_h2)

question: How does narrative analysis differ from thematic analysis?

options.A: Narrative analysis relies entirely on laboratory blood work and numerical statistics
options.B: Narrative analysis looks at complete individual life stories rather than breaking text into codes
options.C: Narrative analysis only uses closed-ended survey questions with fixed answers
options.D: Narrative analysis avoids recording interviews and relies on memory alone

explanation: Narrative analysis keeps a person's life story in chronological order rather than chopping the text up into separate codes. [learn more](BMP225_U1_T3#BMP225_U1_T3_h4)

question: Under the NYHA classification, how is a pregnant woman categorized if she has heart symptoms while completely at rest?

options.A: Class four
options.B: Class three
options.C: Class one
options.D: Class two

explanation: Class four is the most severe category, assigned when heart failure symptoms happen even while the patient is resting. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T4#BMP221_U4_T4_h2)

question: Which anatomical structure is blocked or cut during female sterilization surgery?

options.A: The Vagina and fornix
options.B: The Ovaries and follicles
options.C: The Uterine cervix
options.D: The Fallopian tubes

explanation: Tubal ligation physically blocks the fallopian tubes so that sperm cannot travel upward to fertilize an egg released from the ovary. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T5#BMP126_U2_T5_h3)

question: How does chronic lung injury from oxygen and mechanical pressure present in a former preterm infant?

options.A: Inability to swallow milk safely
options.B: Sudden enlargement of the right lung only
options.C: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia with ongoing breathing difficulties
options.D: Complete absence of breath sounds on both sides

explanation: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia happens due to long-term damage to delicate lung structures, leaving infants needing extra oxygen and prone to breathing challenges. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T5#BMP220_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is a major difference between typical and atypical antipsychotics?

options.A: Atypical agents generally carry a lower risk of extrapyramidal movement side effects
options.B: Typical agents are completely safe during pregnancy unlike atypical agents
options.C: Typical agents do not cross the blood-brain barrier

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical symptom of apnea of prematurity?

options.A: Bluish discoloration around the lips or face
options.B: Pauses in breathing lasting over 20 seconds
options.C: Slowing of the heart rate or bradycardia
options.D: Continuous high fever and sweating

explanation: Apnea involves sudden breathing cessation and slow heart rate, not persistent high fever and sweating. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T1#BMP220_U1_T1_h7)

question: Why do midwives take a patient history and do a physical check at every antenatal visit?

options.A: To check for genetic issues in the first trimester
options.B: To replace the need for lab tests
options.C: To fill out clinic paperwork
options.D: To get a complete picture of mother and baby health

explanation: Combining history and physical checks gives the midwife complete information to keep both mother and baby safe. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why might a patient with hypothyroidism gain weight even with a poor appetite?

options.A: Hypothyroidism triggers an uncontrollable urge to eat in secret
options.B: The digestive system absorbs every single calorie without any waste
options.C: Fluid retention in the abdomen mimics rapid weight gain from fat
options.D: The body's metabolic rate is so slow that it burns very few calories

explanation: Even with reduced food intake, a severely depressed metabolism means calories are burned very slowly, leading to weight gain. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T6#BMP216_U2_T6_h4)

question: How does living alone commonly affect the dietary habits of older adults?

options.A: It improves their cooking skills because they have more free time
options.B: It causes them to spend all their money on expensive supplements
options.C: It forces them to eat five large meals a day with neighbors
options.D: It reduces their motivation to cook and eat varied meals

explanation: Eating is often a social activity; when people live or eat alone, the effort of preparing food often leads to skipping meals or eating poorly. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T7#BMP118_U3_T7_h5)

question: Why is it important to call the receiving hospital before sending a referral patient?

options.A: To book a private VIP ward for the family
options.B: To make sure the facility has beds, blood, and staff ready
options.C: To negotiate the cost of surgery beforehand
options.D: To check the exact distance in kilometers

explanation: Calling ahead prevents arriving at a referral hospital that is full, locked, or lacking the needed blood products and staff. [learn more](BMP227_U1_T3#BMP227_U1_T3_h4)

question: How does reading previous research help a student midwife choose a methodology?

options.A: It eliminates all possible biases during the data gathering phase
options.B: It automatically guarantees ethical approval from the hospital board
options.C: It shows which data collection tools worked well in past studies
options.D: It dictates the exact number of patients needed for every trial

explanation: Looking at past methods helps students adopt successful study designs and avoid past mistakes. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T1#BMP225_U2_T1_h1)

question: What is the standard duration of the postnatal period following childbirth?

options.A: First three months
options.B: First twelve months
options.C: First seven days
options.D: First six weeks

explanation: The postnatal period, or puerperium, covers the first six weeks after delivery when the mother's body returns to its pre-pregnant state. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T3#BMP126_U1_T3_h4)

question: A patient who had surgery ten days ago suddenly starts bleeding from the wound because of an infection. How is this bleeding classified?

options.A: Primary haemorrhage
options.B: Secondary haemorrhage
options.C: Accidental haemorrhage
options.D: Reactionary haemorrhage

explanation: Bleeding occurring a week or more after surgery, linked to infection or tissue breakdown, is classified as secondary haemorrhage. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T4#BMP120_U4_T4_h2)

question: Why do patients need higher doses of their replacement medication when they fall sick with an infection?

options.A: Infections destroy all the oral medication in the stomach
options.B: Sickness makes the kidneys excrete hormones faster
options.C: The body normally increases cortisol output during physical stress
options.D: Higher doses are needed to kill the invading bacteria

explanation: Healthy bodies produce extra cortisol to handle stress like fever or infection; Addison's patients must artificially mimic this increase. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T7#BMP216_U2_T7_h5)

question: What is the main reason for offering family planning services through Primary Health Care?

options.A: To make services easy to reach close to home
options.B: To stop people from visiting urban hospitals
options.C: To replace routine immunization programs
options.D: To remove the need for community health workers

explanation: Primary Health Care brings essential health services directly to the community level so everyone can access them easily. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T3#BMP224_U1_T3_h1)

question: A young female adolescent is rushed to the emergency ward pale, sweating, with a rapid pulse and heavy bleeding after a secret procedure. What is the immediate priority?

options.A: Interview family members about who performed the act
options.B: Resuscitate for hypovolemic shock and stabilize vitals
options.C: Delay treatment until police permission is documented
options.D: Administer oral iron tablets and discharge home

explanation: Saving the patient's life takes precedence in an emergency, requiring immediate stabilization of blood volume and vital signs. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h4)

question: Who is primarily responsible for making a medical diagnosis and prescribing treatment for postpartum psychosis?

options.A: The hospital pharmacist
options.B: The senior ward maid
options.C: The ward midwife
options.D: The psychiatrist

explanation: Diagnosing mental health conditions and prescribing psychiatric medicines are done by a specialist psychiatrist. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T3#BMP223_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary focus of domiciliary midwifery care?

options.A: Managing high-risk surgical cases at home
options.B: Replacing tertiary hospitals in rural districts
options.C: Supervising traditional birth attendant training programs
options.D: Providing maternal and newborn care in the community

explanation: Domiciliary midwifery brings basic, safe maternal and newborn services directly to households and communities where women live. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T2#BMP316_U1_T2_h1)

question: What term describes passing an infection from a mother to her baby during pregnancy or childbirth?

options.A: Latent infection
options.B: Vertical transmission
options.C: Horizontal spread
options.D: Secondary invasion

explanation: Vertical transmission specifically refers to the passage of pathogens from mother to child during the perinatal period. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h2)

question: A baby is born vaginally as a frank breech, is floppy, and has a slow heart rate. What is the immediate priority?

options.A: Administer intravenous oxytocin to the mother to stop bleeding
options.B: Transfer the mother and baby immediately to the surgical theatre
options.C: Initiate neonatal resuscitation according to standard guidelines
options.D: Perform radiological imaging to rule out skeletal fractures

explanation: Any newborn who is struggling after a breech delivery needs quick resuscitation to help them breathe and stabilize their circulation. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T5#BMP311_U1_T5_h7)

question: What term describes an increase in the physical size of a child's body?

options.A: Adaptation
options.B: Maturation
options.C: Development
options.D: Growth

explanation: Growth strictly measures physical changes like height, weight, and organ size rather than functional changes. [learn more](BMP222_U1_T1#BMP222_U1_T1_h1)

question: What happens to a baby when the mother has long-term high blood glucose levels?

options.A: Premature closure of the ductus arteriosus
options.B: Complete cessation of fetal growth
options.C: Fetal hyperinsulinemia
options.D: Severe intrauterine dehydration

explanation: Excess sugar crosses the placenta into the baby, causing the baby's pancreas to produce extra insulin, which leads to extra fat storage and a larger baby. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T2#BMP221_U4_T2_h7)

question: What is the benefit of including experienced mothers in peer counseling sessions?

options.A: They take over the clinical examinations from the midwife
options.B: They handle the documentation of all medical records
options.C: They provide financial loans to pregnant women in need
options.D: They share relatable stories that help reduce cultural fears

explanation: Peers offer trusted, lived experiences that resonate deeply with pregnant women and encourage healthy practices. [learn more](BMP227_U1_T1#BMP227_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why does acalculous cholecystitis happen in very sick patients who do not have gallstones?

options.A: Intravenous antibiotics directly damage the mucosal wall
options.B: Prolonged fasting causes bile stasis and gallbladder ischemia
options.C: High fever melts the natural fats stored in the bile duct
options.D: Frequent blood transfusions block the hepatic portal vein

explanation: When patients are very sick and not eating, bile sits still and the gallbladder does not empty, leading to swelling and tissue damage without any stones. [learn more](BMP125_U4_T4#BMP125_U4_T4_h1)

question: A midwife refuses to give family planning advice to an unmarried teenager, stating it encourages promiscuity. What is this?

options.A: Provider bias and stigma
options.B: Emergency triage management
options.C: Strict confidentiality enforcement
options.D: Standard clinical protocol

explanation: Allowing personal moral judgments to interfere with patient care is provider bias and violates patient rights. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T5#BMP320_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why do midwives move the limbs of an unconscious patient through gentle stretches?

options.A: To keep joints from getting stiff and maintain flexibility
options.B: To make the patient start moving on their own
options.C: To replace the need for turning them in bed
options.D: To build up the patient's muscle strength

explanation: Since the patient cannot move themselves, gentle passive stretches keep the joints flexible and stop contractures. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T1#BMP120_U5_T1_h7)

question: Which piece of protective gear specifically shields the midwife's eyes from sudden fluid spurts during delivery?

options.A: A standard surgical face mask
options.B: Face shields or protective goggles
options.C: Heavy rubber utility boots
options.D: A waterproof plastic apron

explanation: Masks cover the nose and mouth, but goggles or face shields are needed to protect the mucous membranes of the eyes from splashes. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T4#BMP211_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why does blocking sodium channels stop a patient from feeling pain?

options.A: It destroys the local blood supply to the painful area
options.B: It forces the heart to pump blood at a much faster rate
options.C: It stops electrical nerve impulses from traveling to the brain
options.D: It immediately cools down the skin tissue around the wound

explanation: Without sodium movement, nerve fibers cannot carry pain messages upward to the central nervous system. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T5#BMP124_U3_T5_h4)

question: Which of the following describes a key responsibility of the midwife when handling a client with multiple health conditions?

options.A: Coordinating care and documenting clinical findings clearly for referral
options.B: Ordering major surgical operations independently
options.C: Purchasing specialized foreign drugs using personal funds
options.D: Diagnosing rare genetic disorders using laboratory microscopes

explanation: Midwives bridge the gap between clients and specialized medical officers by providing accurate documentation and structured referrals. [learn more](BMP224_U2_T3#BMP224_U2_T3_h6)

question: What substance is stored in platelet granules to help attract other platelets to a site of injury?

options.A: Immunoglobulin
options.B: Hemoglobin
options.C: Adenosine diphosphate
options.D: Albumin

explanation: Platelets release adenosine diphosphate from their granules to signal nearby platelets to help form a plug. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T4#BMP111_U5_T4_h3)

question: What usually happens when the normal acid level in the vagina drops?

options.A: Fungal spores grow faster inside the uterus.
options.B: Normal bacteria are completely destroyed by a drop in body temperature.
options.C: Harmful bacteria multiply quickly when protective lactic acid goes down.
options.D: Lactobacilli need an alkaline environment to make hydrogen peroxide.

explanation: Lactobacilli keep the vaginal environment acidic and safe; when they decrease, harmful bacteria can take over. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h1)

question: How does work positively influence a person's life?

options.A: By completely eliminating the risk of developing chronic illnesses
options.B: By ensuring the worker never experiences physical fatigue
options.C: By replacing the need for community healthcare services
options.D: By providing financial security, social connection, and purpose

explanation: Employment offers many non-financial benefits that contribute positively to overall human well-being. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T1#BMP126_U4_T1_h2)

question: How does the amount of endometrial tissue relate to the pain a patient feels?

options.A: Pain intensity does not always match the physical volume of lesions
options.B: Extensive scarring always produces absolute paralysis in the limbs
options.C: Mild symptoms guarantee that zero pelvic adhesions exist
options.D: Small lesions never cause any noticeable discomfort whatsoever

explanation: A person can have just a few small spots and feel terrible pain, or have a lot of tissue growth with very little pain. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T8#BMP310_U3_T8_h3)

question: Which bone feature is commonly found in an anthropoid pelvis?

options.A: Prominent ischial spines
options.B: A side-to-side inlet wider than the front-to-back
options.C: A very wide subpubic arch
options.D: A short sacrum with four segments

question: An infant weighs 5 kg. The safe dose is 4 mg/kg. What is the total dose to administer?

options.A: 20 mg
options.B: 54 mg
options.D: 9 mg

explanation: Multiply the child's weight in kilograms (5) by the prescribed dose per kilogram (4) to get 20 mg. [learn more](BMP120_U2_T6#BMP120_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why are frequent, small meals often recommended for patients with liver cirrhosis?

options.A: They force the gallbladder to empty stored bile continuously
options.B: They completely cure portal hypertension within a few days
options.C: They stop the stomach from producing any digestive acids
options.D: They prevent overloading a compromised metabolism while ensuring adequate calories

explanation: Because their metabolism is strained and appetite is usually low, eating smaller meals helps these patients get enough nutrition without tiring out their system. [learn more](BMP125_U4_T2#BMP125_U4_T2_h6)

question: What fluid builds up inside the brain ventricles of a newborn with hydrocephalus?

options.A: Extracellular matrix
options.B: Amniotic fluid
options.C: Cerebrospinal fluid
options.D: Venous whole blood

explanation: Hydrocephalus specifically involves the excess accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid within the ventricular spaces of the brain. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T7#BMP220_U2_T7_h1)

question: What must a consent form explicitly state regarding a participant's right to leave the study?

options.A: Participants need formal approval from the hospital ethics committee before leaving
options.B: Participants can only withdraw if they find a replacement to take their place
options.C: Participants must finish the full study period to receive any financial compensation
options.D: Participants can withdraw at any time without losing their standard medical care

explanation: Participation is completely voluntary, and individuals must always be free to exit a study whenever they choose without penalty to their healthcare. [learn more](BMP225_U1_T7#BMP225_U1_T7_h4)

question: Which two standard views are taken during a screening mammogram?

options.A: Superior and inferior tangential
options.B: Anteroposterior and posteroanterior
options.C: Craniocaudal and mediolateral oblique
options.D: Transverse and longitudinal sagittal

explanation: The craniocaudal (top-down) and mediolateral oblique (angled side view) ensure nearly all breast and axillary tissue is imaged. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T3#BMP320_U2_T3_h4)

question: A patient wants to buy strong antibiotics over the counter for a mild cold. What is the main danger of this practice?

options.A: Causing an immediate allergic reaction in the liver tissue
options.B: Promoting drug-resistant strains of bacteria in the community
options.C: Lowering the patient's normal body temperature too quickly
options.D: Killing all beneficial fungi in the upper respiratory tract

explanation: Using antibiotics when they are not needed exposes normal bacteria to the drug, allowing resistant strains to survive, multiply, and spread. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T1#BMP124_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is NOT a recommended strategy for midwives working to reduce mental health stigma?

options.A: Educating community members about the medical basis of mental illness
options.B: Treating psychological issues as personal weaknesses or spiritual flaws
options.C: Providing compassionate, non-judgmental care during checkups
options.D: Normalizing conversations about emotional wellbeing in antenatal classes

explanation: Labeling mental health conditions as personal weaknesses builds stigma and stops women from seeking help. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T7#BMP223_U3_T7_h7)

question: Why is a low hemoglobin test result alone sometimes insufficient to diagnose the exact root cause of maternal anemia in Nigeria?

options.A: Laboratory reagents in local clinics are specifically designed to give false readings.

options.C: Conditions like malaria and hookworm often co-exist and also cause low blood counts.
options.D: Hemoglobin levels naturally fluctuate wildly every single hour of the day.

explanation: Anemia in tropical regions is often multifactorial, involving iron deficiency alongside malaria hemolysis, hookworm blood loss, or other nutritional shortages. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T9#BMP118_U2_T9_h5)

question: What birth weight percentile marks the threshold for a newborn to be classified as Small for Gestational Age?

options.A: Above the 90th percentile

options.C: Between the 50th and 75th percentiles
options.D: Below the 10th percentile

question: Which body areas are typically affected by the rash seen in secondary syphilis?

options.C: The scalp and behind the human ears
options.D: Palms of the hands and soles of the feet

question: Why is family involvement considered central to early intervention programs?

options.A: Therapeutic activities are most effective when practiced consistently during daily home routines
options.B: Clinics lack enough space to store toys and therapy equipment
options.C: Specialist therapists only visit clinics once every three years
options.D: Parents must pay all the financial costs of running the clinic

explanation: Children learn best through continuous, everyday practice embedded in natural family interactions rather than isolated weekly clinic sessions. [learn more](BMP222_U1_T4#BMP222_U1_T4_h6)

question: What crucial detail must be recorded alongside the baby's weight and gender in the delivery register?

options.A: Type of labor bed used
options.B: Father's occupation
options.C: Exact time of birth
options.D: Mother's blood group

explanation: The exact time of birth is a legal and clinical necessity needed for tracking medication schedules, pediatric assessments, and developmental milestones. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T3#BMP212_U3_T3_h6)

question: What are 'clue cells' when seen under a microscope?

options.A: White blood cells fighting a fungal infection

options.C: Spores formed by parasites
options.D: Immature cells shed quickly from an inflamed cervix

question: What causes normal skin changes like spider veins and red palms during pregnancy?

options.A: Low circulating cortisol
options.B: Elevated estrogen levels
options.C: Deficiencies in dietary iron
options.D: High parathyroid activity

question: Which of these is NOT a common physical sign of andropause?

options.A: Sudden permanent blindness
options.B: Loss of muscle mass
options.C: Reduced morning erections
options.D: Persistent physical fatigue

question: Why is magnesium sulfate preferred over standard anticonvulsants for preeclampsia?

options.A: It protects the brain and stops fits without deep sedation
options.B: It completely eliminates the need to monitor blood pressure
options.C: It cures the underlying placental disease instantly
options.D: It works faster when given by mouth than other drugs

explanation: The drug targets the nervous system effectively while keeping the mother alert enough to be assessed. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T5#BMP213_U3_T5_h1)

question: A patient has alkaline urine and a history of forming kidney stones along with a bladder infection. Which germ is likely responsible?

options.A: Escherichia coli
options.B: Lactobacillus acidophilus
options.C: Proteus mirabilis
options.D: Bacteroides fragilis

question: Why is a urinary catheter put in before a caesarean section?

options.A: To monitor daily fluid intake and output throughout labor
options.B: To prevent the development of a permanent urinary tract infection
options.C: To speed up the natural involution of the postpartum uterus
options.D: To keep the bladder empty and away from the surgical field

explanation: An empty bladder reduces the risk of accidental surgical injury during the creation of the uterine incision. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T4#BMP311_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which instruction is most important to include in discharge teaching to prevent future episodes of HHS?

options.A: Stop taking all oral medications if feeling tired
options.B: Drink plenty of water and manage early infections
options.C: Avoid eating any carbohydrates for the rest of life
options.D: Check blood pressure only once every six months

explanation: Staying well-hydrated and treating infections early helps prevent the dehydration and stress that trigger HHS. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T4#BMP216_U2_T4_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT typically included in the comprehensive scope of family planning services?

options.A: Offering pre-conception health screening for couples
options.B: Performing major orthopedic surgeries for injured patients
options.C: Providing youth-friendly adolescent reproductive education
options.D: Screening and treating sexually transmitted infections

question: During which stage of pregnancy does heartburn most commonly happen?

question: Why is it important to inspect the delivered placenta and membranes thoroughly?

question: Which area of the lower urinary tract has a high density of estrogen receptors, similar to the vagina?

options.D: Bladder trigone and urethra

question: What main immune substance is found in very high amounts in colostrum?

options.A: Folic acid
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Caseinogen
options.D: Secretory IgA

explanation: Colostrum is rich in secretory IgA, which helps protect the newborn's gut and mucous membranes from germs. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T1#BMP214_U3_T1_h5)

question: When is the best time of day for a pregnant patient to use a prescribed vaginal antifungal pessary?

options.A: Right before going to bed at night
options.B: Immediately after eating morning breakfast
options.C: Mid-afternoon while sitting at work
options.D: Just before doing heavy household chores

explanation: Inserting pessaries at bedtime allows the medication to dissolve and stay in contact with the vaginal walls overnight without leaking out. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T8#BMP124_U4_T8_h5)

question: Why might a menopausal woman have urinary symptoms that feel like an infection even when her urine culture is sterile?

options.A: Rapid hypertrophy of the detrusor muscle walls

options.C: Thinning of the urethral mucosa and reduced closure pressure

question: A midwife is reviewing the forearm anatomy and the interosseous membrane between the radius and ulna. What is a key structural role of this membrane?

options.A: Acting as a primary site for red blood cell production

options.C: Allowing the complete separation of the forearm bones
options.D: Serving as a muscle attachment site and keeping bones aligned

question: Which principle means a client chooses a method freely without any pressure from the midwife?

options.A: Confidentiality
options.B: Voluntarism
options.C: Standardization
options.D: Beneficence

question: How do lower genital tract bacteria typically reach the upper uterus during a medical procedure?

question: Which situation represents a serious legal and ethical breach in nursing documentation?

options.D: Backdating an entry to cover up missed care

question: At 38 weeks, you feel no fetal head or breech in the lower abdomen. What should you do next?

question: Which receptor type causes the uterine muscle to relax when stimulated?

question: Why is the QRS complex much taller and sharper than the P wave on an ECG recording?

options.C: The ventricles contain vastly more muscle mass than the atria
options.D: The QRS complex records repolarization instead of depolarization

question: How does dropping estrogen levels affect the pelvis during midlife?

options.D: It triggers rapid overproduction of endometrial lining

question: Which task is considered a core clinical responsibility in an occupational health clinic?

options.D: Providing immediate first aid and treating minor ailments

question: Which specific finding on a urine test shows that an infection has reached the kidneys rather than staying in the bladder?

question: During which postpartum period do nursing mothers most commonly experience mastitis?

question: How should a midwife handle a local cultural belief that prevents a pregnant woman from eating nutritious foods like eggs?

question: What additional public health step is essential when treating a client diagnosed with gonorrhoea?

question: What advice should a midwife give a pregnant woman regarding meat consumption?

question: A pregnant patient with persistent asthma expresses fear that using her prescribed steroid inhaler will cause birth defects. How should the midwife respond?

options.B: Explain that poorly controlled asthma causes low oxygen that is much more dangerous to the baby than the inhaler

question: Which swelling finding is most concerning and requires an immediate check for pre-eclampsia?

question: Which situation requires an immediate hospital referral during a community growth monitoring session?

question: At how many weeks of pregnancy does bleeding from the birth canal officially count as antepartum haemorrhage (APH)?

question: Why do we check blood grouping and Rh factor for a woman with a threatened miscarriage?

question: What tool or protocol guides the school nurse in handling common minor ailments on campus?

question: You are handling three patients at once: a woman in early latent labor, a woman with a severe headache and high protein in her urine, and a mother wanting a routine check. Who should you see first?

question: A student midwife wants to display booking weights of pregnant women grouped into intervals. Which graph should she choose?

question: How does the sacrum usually look in an anthropoid pelvis?

question: What is the primary way helminths survive inside a human host?

question: Which behavior marks the typical onset of true expressive language in a twelve-month-old child?

question: How does an organized client flow benefit a family planning clinic?

question: Besides pelvic pressure, what common factor worsens hemorrhoids in pregnancy?

question: What is an important clinical fact about the decrease in bone mineral density associated with long-term DMPA use?

question: Which breastfeeding position works best for a mother recovering from a recent Caesarean section to protect her abdominal wound?

question: A traditional birth attendant in a rural village is helping a woman with prolonged labor. What is the best action for the birth attendant to take?

question: How do small pulmonary blood vessels react when an area of the lung has very low oxygen levels?

options.A: They rupture
options.B: They multiply
options.C: They constrict
options.D: They dilate

explanation: Hypoxic vasoconstriction causes local vessels to narrow so blood is sent to healthier parts of the lung where oxygen is available. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T18#BMP111_U5_T18_h5)

question: A patient with HELLP syndrome has a blood pressure of 170/115 mmHg. What is the most appropriate immediate medical action?

options.A: Restrict all oral and intravenous fluids completely
options.B: Wait two hours to see if blood pressure drops on its own
options.C: Administer an intravenous antihypertensive medication
options.D: Encourage ambulation to help lower the blood pressure

explanation: Severe hypertension in pregnancy requires prompt pharmacological reduction to prevent intracranial hemorrhage and stroke. [learn more](BMP221_U3_T6#BMP221_U3_T6_h3)

question: What term describes the practice of assigning unpleasant ward chores to junior staff simply to avoid doing them yourself?
